newsitem.title: USA: Kaiser Aluminum sets cost cuts in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Kaiser Aluminum sets cost cuts in 1997.

text.p: Kaiser Aluminum Corp., one of the world's largest aluminum producers, said Tuesday it aims to cut costs and improve profits significantly by the end of 1997, with the full effect to be felt in 1998 and beyond.
The company, which warned Monday that it will post a loss for the third and possibly fourth quarters, said it disclosed the goal to employees in an internal memo.
Kaiser, which is about 62 percent owned by MAXXAM Inc., attributed the anticipated loss to low prices for alumina and primary aluminum.

Kaiser said it is developing plans to identify how each of its facilities and departments may be able to contribute to its cost-cutting goal. These include possible reductions in production costs; improvements in operating efficiencies; decreases in corporate selling, general and administrative expenses; and enhancements to its product mix.

"The initiative is based on the company's conclusion that the current level of performance of its existing facilities and businesses will not achieve the level of profits the company considers satisfactory based on historic long-term average prices for primary aluminum and alumina," Kaiser said in a brief statement.

Kaiser said Monday it will report a third-quarter loss of 14 cents to 20 cents per share, compared with a profit of 13 cents per share for the year-ago period. It reported profits of 8.2 million, or 9 cents a share, on sales of $567.6 million in the second quarter ended June 30.
Kaiser's stock fell 12.5 cents to $10.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
